content.text: ▪︎often d/t lifting/twisting injuries or strenuous activity
▪︎back pain: most cases self-limited; 90% resolve w/in 6wks of tx
▪︎malignancy: unexplained wt loss, failure to improve w/ tx, pain >6wks, pain at rest or night + hx of CA or age >50 → further w/u
▪︎infection/epidural abscess: fever, pain at rest, recent infection or surg, immunocompromised, IVDU
▪︎back pain + fever + neuro deficits: epidural abscess
▪︎other serious causes of back pain: AAA or dissection, PUD, kidney stones, pyelonephritis, pancreatitis
▪︎nonopioid tx 1st-line for nonspecific muscular back pain
▪︎strain of cervical paraspinal muscles; often hx of minor precipitating injury, but can occur from everyday stressors (poor posture or sleep habits)
▪︎PE: tenderness of neck paraspinal + trapezius muscles w/o radicular sx; full but painful ROM
▪︎⍉neuro deficits or extremity weakness → if present, w/u other etiologies

▪︎red flags: recent major trauma, weakness, gait changes, bowel or bladder dysfx, Lhermitte phenomenon, fever or chills, IVDU, immunosuppression, unexplained wt loss, hx of CA, visual changes, anterior neck pain
▪︎XR ⍉recommended for acute nontraumatic neck pain; XR if persistent mod–severe pain >6wks or interferes w/ sleep, work, or ADLs
▪︎MRI: red flags, mod–severe pain ⍉responding to conservative mgmt in 6wks, or progressive neuro dysfx
▪︎most mild–mod strains resolve w/ conservative mgmt over 6wks; pain + stiffness can last up to 6wks
▪︎conservative: pt education + reassurance, home exercise program, heat or cold, posture modification (sitting/standing; sleep w/ neck aligned w/ body)
▪︎home exercise: early mobilization + gentle stretching to maintain ROM
▪︎nonbenzodiazepine skeletal muscle relaxant: sx not controlled w/ nonopioid analgesics or cervical spasm
▪︎tramadol: only if inadequate control w/ NSAIDs, APAP, or muscle relaxants; never initial tx
▪︎injury to a musculotendinous unit; often from violent contraction or excessive stretching
▪︎grade 1: minor fiber tearing, mild tenderness or swelling, minimal fx loss
▪︎grade 2: partial tearing, mod pain, swelling, bruising, strength loss
▪︎grade 3: complete tear w/ separation of muscle or tendon; possible palpable defect or avulsion frx
▪︎localized pain, swelling, bruising, loss of fx
▪︎pain ⇡ w/ muscle use, stretching, or direct pressure
▪︎complete rupture: may have visible or palpable muscle deformity
▪︎intercostal strain: tenderness over the muscle; ⇡ w/ stretching it (eg deep breath)
▪︎US or MRI to confirm complete tears (esp complex or delayed cases)
▪︎grade 1–2: rest, ice, NSAIDs, gradual return to activity
▪︎grade 3: ED mgmt + early ortho referral; some need surgical repair or immobilization
▪︎early mobilization once pain allows full ROM + muscle use
